acceptance.given: An SM-2 evaluation presents a case explicitly marked unexecuted.

oracle.expected: The semantic gate emits a rejected-success outcome for that case and records the rejection reason as unexecuted-case.
forbidden: The case is accepted as successful.
The gate omits an unexecuted-case rejection.
oracle.observable: Structured validator result from the existing semantic evaluation validator, including case execution status and success decision.

acceptance.then: Evaluate the unexecuted-case through the repository semantic gate and inspect its structured result.
acceptance.when: During SM-2 adversarial-case validation of an unexecuted case.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A fixture or validator input marks a case unexecuted while the success decision is accepted; the semantic gate must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce SM-2 rejection of success whenever the evaluated case has no execution evidence; preserve the explicit unexecuted-case reason in the structured result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema change; rollback restores the prior semantic-gate decision logic.

slice_hint.state_transition: unexecuted case presented -> semantic gate evaluates execution evidence -> success rejected with reason -> structured result emitted
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The structured result contains a non-success decision for the unexecuted case and an explicit unexecuted-case rejection reason.

acceptance.given: The SM-1 atomic-obligation inventory and its Exact Cover graph are available for evaluation.

oracle.expected: The integrity report contains orphan_count equal to 0 and every atomic obligation is connected bidirectionally to its required witness/consumer coverage.
forbidden: Any atomic obligation lacks a required witness or reverse coverage edge.
The report claims zero orphans without evaluating the inventory graph.
oracle.observable: Structured SM-1 inventory-integrity report produced by the Exact Cover validator.

acceptance.then: Run the Exact Cover inventory integrity evaluation and inspect the emitted orphan count and bidirectional coverage fields.
acceptance.when: When SM-1 inventory integrity is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: An inventory fixture contains an atomic obligation with no covering witness or reverse edge; the integrity validator must report a nonzero orphan count.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Produce an auditable SM-1 integrity result that computes orphan_count from bidirectional Exact Cover and required-witness relationships instead of trusting a declared zero.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema change; rollback restores the prior inventory-evaluation implementation.

slice_hint.state_transition: inventory and graph loaded -> coverage edges and witnesses evaluated -> orphan count calculated -> integrity report emitted
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The report computes orphan_count equal to zero only when every atomic obligation has bidirectional coverage and required witnesses; otherwise validation fails.

acceptance.given: A Consumer has a recorded verdict and diagnostic baseline before enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable are invoked through its real repository call surface.

oracle.expected: After the complete sequence, the Consumer's verdict and diagnostic outputs equal the pre-sequence baseline and the prior route identity is restored.
forbidden: Verdict output differs from the pre-sequence baseline.
Diagnostic output differs from the pre-sequence baseline.
The sequence bypasses the real Consumer call surface or omits restoration.
oracle.observable: Structured Consumer replay result containing pre/post route identity, verdict, and diagnostic values.

acceptance.then: Execute enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through the real Consumer call surface, then compare route identity, verdict, and diagnostics with the captured baseline.
acceptance.when: After completion of the FR-10 operation sequence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A replay fixture mutates the post-sequence verdict or diagnostic baseline; the Consumer replay check must fail.

affected_subjects: Consumer verdict and diagnostic baseline restoration
slice_hint.behavior_change: Make the replay Consumer check capture the pre-sequence route/verdict/diagnostic baseline and require exact equality after enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through real call surfaces.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema change; rollback restores prior Consumer replay sequencing and comparison.

slice_hint.state_transition: baseline captured -> enable -> disable -> behavioral rollback -> re-enable -> route/verdict/diagnostic outputs compared -> restored or rejected
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Replay succeeds only when post-sequence route identity, verdict, and diagnostic outputs exactly match the captured baseline; any mismatch is a failed result.

acceptance.given: An aggregate execution is started with an applicable finite output bound and an observable output counter.

oracle.expected: The aggregate terminates with recorded output at or below its configured bound; budget exhaustion or an exceeded bound is unsuccessful.
forbidden: Recorded output exceeds the applicable bound.
Bound exhaustion is reported as success.
oracle.observable: Aggregate execution record containing configured output bound, emitted-output count, terminal status, and bound-exhaustion reason when applicable.

acceptance.then: Run the aggregate under its configured output budget and inspect the terminal execution record.
acceptance.when: At aggregate execution start and terminal evaluation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: An aggregate fixture emits beyond its configured output bound or exhausts the budget; the bounded-output check must terminate unsuccessfully.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a finite per-aggregate output budget, count emitted output, terminate deterministically on exhaustion, and mark bound exhaustion unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema change; rollback restores previous aggregate execution and probe behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate starts with bound -> output counted -> within-bound terminal success or bound exhaustion -> deterministic unsuccessful terminal record
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every aggregate terminal record has emitted_output_count <= output_bound; any bound exhaustion yields unsuccessful status and a deterministic reason.
